title: Arcee AI Pricing: Models and Cost per Token (2026)
summary: Arcee AI pricing in 2026 breaks down costs for each model tier. Compare the prices to select which plan offers the best value for your use case.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and usage limits


Four costs move an Arcee AI bill. They are the free-tier allowance, the ceilings on requests and context, the gap between input and output pricing, and the absence of any documented discount for bulk work.


The checklist below covers what to confirm before you commit to a monthly volume, and the sections after it expand each item.


- A context cap limits how much of a long document fits in one request, so oversized inputs must be split and the same text gets billed more than once.
- Rate limits cap how fast you can spend, so a heavy batch job may need to run over days rather than hours.
- Output tokens cost more than input tokens, so generation-heavy workloads cost more than their input volume suggests.
- Arcee documents no batch or cache discount, so budget at the full list rate.


I couldn't confirm a current free allowance or whether starting credits expire.


Treat any trial balance as a test budget and not as offset against production. If credits lapse on a schedule, the first invoice arrives sooner than a forecast built on a free runway would suggest.


### Arcee AI API rate limits and context limits


Check the ceilings for the specific model and route you'll use: Arcee meters limits per request and per minute, and ceilings differ across the places that offer Arcee models. A low ceiling forces queuing or a higher tier.


When a context cap forces long inputs to be chunked, chunking re-sends shared instructions with every integration, so billed input exceeds the raw document size.


Chunking also turns one call into several steps, and that is where the orchestration meter starts to matter.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) charges 1 credit per flow run, whether the flow has two steps or ten, so breaking a long document into smaller, more dependable calls adds nothing to that side of the bill.


Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module, so each extra step there is another charge, and the careful splitting is what gets taxed.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production, and the Arcee tokens still bill at the rates above.


I found no documented batch discount and no prompt-caching discount. Competing vendors often halve the price of asynchronous work or discount repeated prefixes, so the absence matters.


A workload that resends a long system prompt on every call pays for it in full each time. Until Arcee documents otherwise, model that repetition at the standard input rate.


### Self-hosting and marketplace compute


If you run the weights yourself, per-token metering gives way to rented GPU time, which is billed whether or not requests arrive. That favors steady, high-volume traffic and punishes spiky use, since an idle instance still costs money.


On a marketplace listing, the cloud provider's compute rate comes on top of any software fee. Compare the monthly rental for the hardware that fits your chosen model against the API cost for the same tokens, and include the engineering time to keep it running.
